task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 8, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about Five Lantern Games' revised board-game components and the design and manufacturing choices involved in making pieces easier to distinguish.

facts.text: An August 2026 prototype note records Five Lantern Games designer Nera Selven comparing tokens with different outlines at a trial of the original game Bridge of Five Markets.
The small publisher is run by three co-founders and contracts manufacturing rather than operating its own factory.
The 2023 edition distinguished four player groups mainly by token color.
The proposed edition adds a different outline and printed symbol to each color, allowing more than one way to distinguish the groups.
The game rules and scoring are unchanged in the current prototype.
A 12-person trial included players who said the old colors were difficult for them to distinguish and others without that reported difficulty.
The trial collected comments about recognition and handling, not a population-wide measure of accessibility or learning ability.
Some testers found one new token harder to pick up, prompting a further shape revision.
Selven said, "Making pieces easier to tell apart is not enough if one of them is awkward to move."
The manufacturer quotes $2,300 for new cutting dies plus $2 per box; the quote assumes a production quantity that the publisher has not disclosed.
The publisher has not signed the production order or fixed the final retail price.
It has received 180 refundable preorder deposits of $10, totaling $1,800, not 180 completed full-price sales.
The deposits remain refundable until the publisher confirms the final specification and delivery schedule.
Retailer Omi Valgren says the box must clearly identify the revised edition so buyers know which components they are obtaining.
Valgren said, "The useful change has to be something a customer can identify before opening the box."
The publisher is considering a component-only pack for existing owners but has not set a price or promised compatibility with every earlier printing.
Existing copies are not being recalled, and owners can continue playing under their original rules.
The source record contains no claim that the redesign treats a medical condition or is suitable for every access need.
The company's office shares space with a community arts print room, where early paper prototypes were cut by hand.
The founders have not released a completed cost-recovery forecast or evidence that the redesign has increased retail sales.

forbidden_additions: A finished production run, 180 full-price sales, a fixed delivery date or an old-edition recall
Universal accessibility, therapeutic benefits or a demonstrated retail-sales increase
preserve: If quoted: Making pieces easier to tell apart is not enough if one of them is awkward to move.
If quoted: The useful change has to be something a customer can identify before opening the box.
The design changes identification and handling, not the supplied game rules.
